classify:1.safeSummary:
None of the 129 SQL-text interpolation sites in the 16 files is a suspect. A value from a request, a stored user value, a document, a connector payload or a model reaches SQL text only as a bind parameter.

Placeholder builders (about 90 sites). WHERE clauses are built from fixed column predicates plus "$" + args.length, $${idx++} or $${paramIndex++}, then joined with ' AND '. LIMIT and OFFSET are also placeholders. This covers mdx-audit.ts:102-129, mdx-vault.ts:140-220, global-dossier.service.ts:255-280 and :850, contradiction-engine-service.ts:522 and :945-972, ectd-submission-agent.ts:378-397, notification-service.ts:110-125, cross-jurisdictional-service.ts:179-408, ivd-assessments.service.ts:93-94 and :146-147, and vault-document-index.service.ts:201-237. ORDER BY is always fixed text. ILIKE patterns such as `%${program}%` and `${ctdPrefix}%` are built in JS and pushed as parameters, not written into the SQL text.

Identifiers fixed in code:
- global-dossier.service.ts: `${this.schema}` is a private readonly 'global_dossier' (line 49), about 21 sites.
- register-writes.ts:194: `${register.table}` comes from the PROGRAM_FILED_REGISTERS constant map (lines 166-171). Every caller in server/api/cmc/routes.ts passes a member of that map.
- vault-legal-holds.ts: HOLD_COLUMNS is a constant string (line 34).
- run-control.ts:847: LISTEN ${RUN_CONTROL_CHANNEL} uses the constant 'ana_run_control'.
- investigator-brochure-view-assembler.ts:218-258: regclass, schema, table, orgColumn, domain, name and extra all come from the constant STORE_PROBES array. The cast is either '$1::int' or '$1::text', chosen by an INTEGER_TYPES Set lookup on the catalog's data_type. The org id is the only bound parameter.
- vault-document-index.service.ts:99-110, mdx-vault.ts:218 and vault-relationships.ts:245: DOCUMENT_COLUMNS, TENANT_WHERE, vaultDataEligibleSql('d'), vaultBinaryAvailableSql('d') and supersededSql('o') are code-built fragments with literal aliases.
- lifecycle-signature.ts:82: a boolean ternary that appends either '' or 'FOR SHARE'.

Numeric LIMIT written into the text (ivd-assessments.service.ts:97). The value is `LIMIT ${limit}` with limit = Math.min(500, Math.max(1, opts.limit ?? 100)). The source is req.query.limit run through parseInt(…) || undefined at server/routes/ivd-assessments.ts:101-105, plus a constant 500 from ivd-lifecycle.ts:433. Math.max/Math.min always return a number (or NaN, which only fails as a syntax error), so no text can be injected. It is still the one place in this shard where a request-derived value lands in SQL text instead of a placeholder, so it is worth parameterising for consistency.

drizzle-queryable.ts:40. The adapter passes the caller's statement text through sql.raw and re-binds each $n as sql.param, so it is safe only if callers pass fixed text. The callers I listed (leaf-document-resolver, leaf-source-resolver, estar-submission-service, artifact-signed-act, bundle-executor) pass shared writer statements. I did not deep-trace each caller's text. It is a contract to keep, not a current finding.

All remaining `${…}` hits in these files are inside log, error or description strings, not SQL.

classify:0.safeSummary:
No suspects in this shard. All 86 interpolated SQL-text sites are safe. Breakdown:
(1) Code-constant schema and identifiers. agent-runtime.service.ts has 37 uses of ${this.schema}, a private readonly 'agent_runtime' (line 54). reg-change-service.ts:116/134/146 uses SELECT_COLS, a module constant (line 76). mdx-health.service.ts:220 uses `FROM ${name}`, and the only caller is the hardcoded PROBED_TABLES list (line 274), which is also checked first with to_regclass($1).
(2) Placeholder builders. agent-runtime has 12 `$${paramIndex++}` sites and 4 whereClause sites built only from constant fragments plus placeholders. authoring-plan-generator.ts:1100-1111/1118/1124 and org-readiness-overview.ts:267-276 build filters as `$${params.length}` with constant fragments. regulatory-delta-radar-service.ts:210/216 builds placeholders as `$${idx+1}`.
(3) Ternaries that pick between fixed strings. ivdr-routes.ts:420/682 (scoped boolean adds ' AND c.program_id = $2'). mdx-ana-drafts.ts:118-119 (programId adds 'AND p.id = $3'; ageClause maps 'today'/'week'/'older' to constant INTERVAL clauses, else ''). authoring-record.ts:163 (order is 'ASC' or 'DESC'). module3-compile.ts:213 (resetApproval = opts.event==='refreshed', a constant SET fragment). documentExportService.ts:790/799 (constant ORDER BY and ANY($n) fragments). authoring-approval-carryover.ts:161 (byId from /^\d+$/ picks between two constant predicates; the value itself is $1). document-chunking.service.ts:309-310 (vec boolean adds constant '$10::vector'/NOW()).
(4) Columns from an allowlist. regulatory-delta-radar-service.ts:215/303/380 interpolate orgColumn and statusColumn. getGuidanceColumns (lines 1132-1158) maps information_schema results through hardcoded ternaries, so the only possible values are 'organization_id', 'org_id', 'status' or 'document_status'. The columns[] array is otherwise constants. The embedding string at line 191 is a bind value, not SQL text.
(5) Numeric coercion. authoring-plan-generator.ts:1120 interpolates LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset}. Both are results of Math.max/Math.min, which always return a JS number (limit clamped to 1-200), so they cannot carry SQL text. The worst case is NaN, Infinity or exponent notation from a non-integer offset, which only causes a syntax error.
(6) Code-generated predicate helpers with a constant alias. document-chunking.service.ts:147 vaultBinaryAvailableSql('d') and document-passage-search.ts:147 vaultDataEligibleSql('d') come from server/services/document-data-disposition/eligibility.ts. The alias is constant and also regex-validated by alias() (/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/i). All other request-, user- or model-derived values in these files reach SQL only as bind parameters.
Hardening note (not a finding): authoring-plan-generator.ts:1120 would be cleaner as bound $n LIMIT/OFFSET with Number.isInteger validation, because a non-integer offset from a caller produces a SQL syntax error rather than a 400.

classify:3.safeSummary:
I found 69 safe sites and 2 latent suspects, both in a service that no route reaches. I read all 18 files and found no exploitable injection that a request can reach.

Safe patterns, by file:
- Placeholder lists built from a counter, with values sent as bind parameters: ai-editing.ts:482/507 (claims and citations); audit-immutability-triggers.ts:132 (`$${i*3+1}::text`); the WHERE filters in mdx-cdx.ts:80-86, commitments-service.ts:283-288, decision-record-service.ts:281-311 and :366-398, and external-intelligence-service.ts:154-167. The LIKE patterns at ai-editing.ts:1439 and :1467 are bind values, not SQL text.
- SET column names looked up in a fixed map in code: mdx-cdx.ts:170-187 and :285-301 (COL map, unmapped keys skipped); decision-record-service.ts:485-505 (iterates the code's `editable` map, never the input's keys); safety-narrative.ts:163/193 (`EDITABLE_CASE_FIELDS[key].column`). In safety-narrative, the `in` check at :143 also accepts prototype keys like `toString`. That only gives `undefined = $n` and a SQL error, never text the attacker controls. It is a robustness nit, not an injection.
- Fixed fragments chosen by a boolean or an enum: module-subscriptions.ts:446-459 (status is checked against an allowlist and the reason is bound); program-access.ts:182 (constant ` AND deleted_at IS NULL`); separation-of-duties.ts:147 (sectionFilter is a constant that uses `$3`); separation-of-duties.ts:267 (SQL comes from the SINGLE_AUTHOR constant map; a prototype key only causes an error); contradiction-resolution-orchestrator.ts:533-548 (table and id column are picked by a ternary from two literals); checkpoint-manager `checkpoint_ns ? 'AND c.channel = $2' : ''`.
- Constants: hf-files-service.ts SELECT_COLS (4 sites); labeling-pi-service.ts SELECT_COLS and DOC_ORDER (6 sites); vault-where-used.ts ESTAR_ATTACHMENT_MATCH, called only with literal record expressions (2 sites); contextual-ingest.ts:167 (`atomOriginalFileAvailableSql('a')` with a literal alias; ctdSection at :194 goes into a bound text[] value, not SQL text); checkpoint-manager `${this.schema}` (about 25 sites; it defaults to 'agent_runtime' and the only constructor, langgraph-orchestrator.service.ts:122, passes no schema).
- ensureCoreTables.ts:395: the schema name comes only from REQUIRED_SCHEMAS = ['public','vault','extensions'] (:43). ensureCoreTables.ts:576 runs CREATE statements from a map in code.
- tenant-full-export.service.ts:350/354: schema, table and tenant column come from the information_schema catalog, are filtered by the TENANT_KEY_COLUMNS/EXPORT_SCHEMAS constants, and are checked against /^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/ and double-quoted. The scoped predicate is an own-key lookup in a frozen map, and LIMIT is a constant.

suspects.source: forkFromCheckpoint(sourceThreadId, checkpointId, newThreadId, createdBy) parameter, server/services/cognitive-ecosystem/checkpoint-manager.service.ts:500-505. No caller anywhere in server/ or shared/. The only consumer, langgraph-orchestrator.service.ts, uses getTuple and put only.
suspects.validation: Partial and incidental. The SELECT at :515 must first find a row with id = $1 (bound) and thread_id = $2. Injection therefore also needs a stored checkpoint id that contains a quote. That is impossible if checkpoints.id is uuid-typed and possible if it is text. No format check is applied before the value is spliced into the string literal.
suspects.reachability: Unreachable today. The cognitive-ecosystem router is retired (server/bootstrap/register-document-routes.ts:253, '#844 Phase 0.2') and server/routes/cognitive-ecosystem.ts imports nothing from the service. It is a latent defect: wiring up any fork endpoint would expose it. The fix is to pass checkpointId as a bind parameter, e.g. jsonb_build_object('forked_from', $4::text).

suspects.expression: whereClause += ` AND c.metadata->>'${key}' = $${paramIndex++}` for each key of options.filter
suspects.source: The keys of options.filter in CheckpointManager.list(config, options), checkpoint-manager.service.ts:172-201. They follow the LangGraph BaseCheckpointSaver list() filter, which is normally caller- or API-supplied. No caller passes a filter today; the only in-repo users of CheckpointManager are getTuple and put (langgraph-orchestrator.service.ts:354, :751).
suspects.validation: None. The key is spliced into a single-quoted SQL literal with no allowlist or escaping. Values are bound.
suspects.reachability: Unreachable today, for the same reason as S3-1 (the cognitive-ecosystem routes are retired, #844). It is latent: any route or agent tool that forwards a user filter object to list() would be a cross-tenant critical injection. The fix is to bind the key too (c.metadata->>$n) or check it against /^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/.

classify:2.safeSummary:
No suspects in this shard. Every interpolation into SQL text in the 17 files is one of the safe forms below, traced to its source.

Found in mdx-ana-memory.ts:87-106 and 259-270, mdx-submission-gateway.ts:140-157, turn-record-verify.ts:242-258 (limit is clamped and passed as a bind), assumption-registry-service.ts:487-515, account-canon.ts:408-521 and 550-635, regulatory-negotiation-logbook-service.ts:262-295, 478-489 and 773-809, federated-learning.service.ts:839-850, project-rollup-service.ts:351-361 (VALUES tuples are all binds). Optional filters with no value are fixed literals (verified/pinned true/false branches).
(2) Column names from hardcoded allowlists, with values bound. assumption-registry-service.ts:316-337 uses a fixed editable map. negotiation-logbook :314-338 and :527-551 use fixed updatableFields arrays. cmc/routes.ts:952 and :979-982 use spec.table, a TS literal union of 5 tables whose call sites at :1107/1192/1292/1604/1695 are literals, plus signing columns and signedValue from code defaults or the constant at :1532. The id is checked as an integer or UUID and is a bind.
(3) Schema/table/fragment constants. federated-learning this.schema='federated_ml' (:67). persistent-queries HASH_CHAIN_TABLE and GENESIS_PREV constants (:106/:110). audit/chain.ts ORDER_SQL constants (:87/:90), with boolean-selected fragments at :648/650/683 and tenantId bound. research-compliance-report-providers countBy(table,col): every call site passes literals and the extra arg is never passed. section-drift sectionFilter is a fixed literal 'AND s.section_key = $3'. document-alias-backfill: hasBinding picks a literal column, and the to_regclass name is a bind. Vault helper SQL builders (supersededSql/currentVersionLateral/capturedDataEligibleSql/capturedBinaryAvailableSql/vaultBinaryAvailableSql) are called with literal aliases. vault-version-checkin adds FOR UPDATE through a boolean.
(4) Numeric LIMIT/OFFSET interpolated as text. In every case the value can only be a number, so it cannot carry SQL:
- account-canon.ts:427 LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset} and :521 LIMIT ${options.limit}. The only caller, routes/account-intelligence.ts:109-110 and :213, uses parseInt(...)||default.
- :574 LIMIT ${maxItems}. From POST /api/account-intelligence/resolve, where zod z.number() means JSON numbers only (non-integers cause a SQL error, not injection). Other callers pass no maxItems.
- negotiation-logbook :780/:812 LIMIT ${options.limit}. The only caller, innovation-routes.ts:1230, uses parseInt(...)||20.
(5) leaf-source-resolver.ts:797-802 uses a drizzle sql`` template, so documentId and organizationId are parameters. Embedding vector strings ([...join(',')]) in the logbook are bound params, not SQL text. Everything else is only in log or error messages.
Outside the injection scope: negotiation-logbook updateThread/updateEntry (:335-341, :549-553) filter by id only, with no organization predicate. They rely on route-level ownership guards (innovation-routes assertChildInOrg pattern), which this pass did not verify.

classify:5.safeSummary:
No suspects in this shard. I checked about 72 places where SQL text is built from interpolated values. I read the dynamic-SQL regions of each file in full and grepped every `${` and string concatenation in all 19 files. Each site fits one of these safe patterns:
(1) Placeholder builders. WHERE filters and SET lists add only `$${args.length}` / `$${paramIndex++}` / `$${o+N}` / `$${i+1}`, and every value goes in as a bind parameter. This covers mdx-labeling, mdx-qms, mdx-rbm (list filters, plus buildPatch at mdx-rbm.ts:123 and the risk_score/residual_score/status/breached additions), project-rules list, update and exec-log, gdpr updateProcessingActivity, compliance-guardrails (listRules, updateRule, profiles, runs, the stats whereClause and its .replace() on fixed column names), cross-artifact-consistency-scanner filters, grants list* builders, the send-message.ts:395/1141 multi-row VALUES, and the working-memory.ts:241-244 INSERT.
(2) Column names inside SET clauses come from hardcoded maps such as COL, ASSESS_COL/ITEM_COL/KRI_COL/QTL_COL/SIGNAL_COL/PLAN_COL/ACTION_COL, the project-rules fieldMap and the gdpr columnMap. Each map is looked up with keys from zod-parsed data (unknown keys are stripped) or from the map's own entries. The working-memory column list is code constants only.
(3) Code constants: MAX_ROWS=200 (artifacts-center:260), QUEUE_LIMIT=200 and SELECT_REQUEST (module-access-requests), COLUMNS (vault-retention-period:92/148), LEGACY_HEAD_ORDER_SQL (chain-row:62), the PRIVILEGE_GUCS frozen list (rlsBypassSession:62), the fixed-SQL strings in the mdx-qms readiness block, PURGE_DOORS columns and fn names, VAULT_DOCUMENT_TENANCY, and PURGE_PARENT_SCOPED predicates.
(4) Ternaries between fixed literals: grants setMilestoneStatusTx (:150) and setInvoiceStatusTx dateCol (:172, which is also gated by the INVOICE_STATUSES allowlist), protocol-development :83 FOR UPDATE, and rules-engine :330 success/failure counter.
(5) Numeric only. cross-artifact-consistency-scanner :347 LIMIT/OFFSET come from Math.max/Math.min, which always return a number (worst case NaN or Infinity, which errors rather than injects). The cerGenerationService :790 sql.raw embeds JSON.stringify of two Number()||0 values only.
(6) tenant-offboarding :423 `DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE ${predicate}`. The table comes from the frozen PURGE_CHILD_TABLES. The childTables override is passed only by tests. A name regex is asserted at :403, and the predicate is looked up as an own key of a frozen map, with a fixed fallback.
Non-SQL interpolations (log text, prompt text, error messages) were not counted.

Two observations outside SQL injection. First, compliance-guardrails updateRule (:358) and the runs/stats queries have no organization predicate; per the rlsBypassSession comment that innovation service is unmounted. Second, the gdpr columnMap includes organizationId as an updatable column (gdprComplianceService.ts:377). That is a possible tenancy/mass-assignment issue depending on the callers, but it is bound as a parameter, not injected.

classify:6.safeSummary:
None of the 18 files has a suspect site. The safe sites fall into these patterns:
(1) Placeholder numbering. `$${params.length}`, `$${idx++}` and `$${paramIndex++}` build WHERE and SET fragments, and every value goes into the bind array. This covers bla-workbench, clinical-operations-routes, project-sections, scim (the filter regex output is bound), pharmacovigilanceService, cognitive-audit, guidance-impact-scanner and account-skill-bundles.
(2) Column names from fixed maps. In mdx-ldt.ts:221-233/294-301 the keys come from a zod-parsed body and are looked up in the COL map. Similarly, account-skill-bundles.ts:117-139 uses fieldMap, and ema-cesp.ts:280-293 uses COL with a patch that the code builds itself. Clinical-ops, project-sections and scim SET clauses use literal column names.
(3) Constants and code-fixed identifiers: `cognitive_audit` from `this.schema`, SELECT_COLS in market-access, SELECT_POLICY in org-placement-writer, the labelCol ternary in network-risk-aggregator.ts:93, the byKey ternary in kit-section-write.ts:105, the stamps ternary in protocol-milestones:44, SECTION_ROW_CAP, and section.ts helpers (actorJoin, isoUtc, utcWallClock), which callers only invoke with literals or integers. document-catalog-search calls vaultDataEligibleSql('d') and supersededSql('d') with a literal; its pgvector literal is passed as bind $2.
(4) LIMIT/OFFSET. guidance-impact-scanner.ts:473-488 runs them through Math.max/Math.min, which always returns a number (NaN at worst, which makes the query error rather than inject). In account-skill-bundles.ts:186/265/355 the value is `options?.limit || 50`, but none of the callers (server/routes/account-intelligence.ts:368/480/546) passes limit, so it is always the constant.
(5) grdheService uses drizzle sql`` tagged templates and composes them as sql`${query} ...`, so values are parameterized. The sql.raw at 1476/1478 is reached only when AUDITABLE_TABLE_SCOPES[tableName].kind === 'tenant'. That fixed map (lines 158-167) means tableName and scope.column can only be real table and column names. A prototype key such as `constructor` would return an object whose kind is undefined, so it never reaches sql.raw.
Two latent hardening notes, neither exploitable today:
- account-skill-bundles.ts:186/265/355 interpolates `options?.limit` unvalidated. It would become injectable if a future caller passed a request value.
- The COL/fieldMap lookups use plain objects without hasOwnProperty. They are safe today because zod strips unknown keys and the ema-cesp patch keys come from code.

The remaining ${} hits are in log, error or audit strings, not SQL. Examples: audit-trail-routes.ts:72, compliance-reviews.ts:259-422, confidenceScoringEngine.ts:143-805, and the multipart body built in rest-gateway-helpers.ts:157-164.

classify:8.safeSummary: I found no request-, document-, connector- or model-controlled value reaching SQL text in any of the 18 files. I checked all 117 non-placeholder interpolations inside SQL-bearing template literals using a TypeScript-AST scan, then read each one in its file. About 100 further sites only build $N placeholders, from $${paramCount}, $${args.length}, $${params.length}, $${idx++} or $${values.push(v)}. There is no sql.raw or sql.identifier in this shard, and no '+' string concatenation with SQL. The safe patterns, by type: (1) WHERE and SET lists assembled from fixed-text fragments plus $N placeholders, with all values bound: mdx-clinical-studies, mdx-ivd-performance, mdx-rbm-data, signedAuditExport, template-registry, advisory-committee-service, templateStore, evidence-spine (where/scopes), and authoring.router (updates at 2082 and 2781, query += at 1015-1412, 3079-3095 and 5432-5449). (2) PATCH column names in mdx-clinical-studies (lines 207-221 and four more handlers) and mdx-ivd-performance (184 and 331) come from a hardcoded COL map keyed by Zod-parsed fields; unknown keys are stripped or skipped. (3) INSERT column lists are code constants with conditional fixed names: authoring-documents 342, evidence-spine 246. (4) Shared predicate helpers take only literal aliases; a repo-wide grep found no non-literal argument: vaultDataEligibleSql, supersededSql, versionCountLateral, VALID_LINK in vault-version-family, captured*Sql, recordedLineage*Sql in derived-impact, sectionHasContentSql. visibleOrgClause and VISIBLE return fixed text plus a placeholder. CLINICAL_SOURCE_TYPES at index.ts:103 is a const tuple. PARENT_COLS in program-journey is a constant. orgFilter at signedAuditExport.ts:265 is a constant. lock at authoring.router.ts:3148 is a boolean picking a fixed string. (5) Inline LIMIT/OFFSET values always come out as a number or NaN (Math.min/Math.max), so they can cause an error but not an injection. In citation-engine.ts:1823 they come from a Zod-parsed query in ana-features.ts:2725. In evidence-spine.service.ts 518/568/642/686/791 they are clamped to 1-500. One side defect: a fractional or NaN limit gives a 500, not an injection. uploadsCap in project-vault is parseInt of an environment variable, clamped and bound as $3.

suspects.expression: `SELECT * FROM ${this.escapeTableName(recordType)} WHERE id = $1` (also UPDATE ${this.escapeTableName(tableName)} SET is_active = FALSE ... WHERE id = $1)
suspects.source: Caller-supplied recordType/tableName parameters of createElectronicSignature, verifySignature (read from compliance.electronic_signatures.record_type), verifyRecordIntegrity and auditedDelete. No caller exists: getCortexComplianceService (:1030) and the class are imported only by the barrel server/services/cortex/index.ts and a smoke test, and nothing imports that barrel.
suspects.validation: A regex only, /^[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+$/. That stops syntax injection but is not an allowlist, so any schema-qualified table name passes (for example another tenant-scoped table or pg_catalog.*). The statements also have no organization predicate, so if this were ever wired to request input it would read, or soft-delete, any row by id in any table the runtime role can reach, subject only to RLS.
suspects.reachability: Currently unreachable: no route, router or tool calls CortexComplianceService. This is a latent identifier-injection pattern; the fix is to replace the regex with a fixed allowlist of table names, or delete the dead service.

classify:10.safeSummary:
I found no suspects in the 19 files: every value from a request, a model or a document is passed as a bind parameter. I found no drizzle sql.raw, sql.identifier or db.execute calls. For AnaToolExecutor.ts (21,768 lines) I used a template-literal scanner plus a search for .query(<variable>) and += string building. I read the other 18 files at every site that interpolates into SQL, not line by line.

Safe patterns seen:
(1) Placeholder building. $${args.length}, $${paramIdx++}, $${o + n} and $${offset + n} build multi-row VALUES and dynamic WHERE lists. Values always go in args. Seen in ectd/routes.ts:263, evidence-ask.ts:308/324, knowledgeGraphService.ts:187/208, citation-search.ts:157-170, mdx-udi.ts:319-329, regulatory-correspondence.ts:778-786/1023-1027, confidence-calibration:112-131/316, ema-question-taxonomy:116-144, changeControl.service.ts:168-172, source-usage.service.ts:526-557/697-719, AnaToolExecutor list_vault_documents (~20436-20455) and list_governed_documents (~20585-20597).
(2) Dynamic SET lists where the column names come from a fixed COL map in code and unknown keys are dropped: mdx-udi.ts:420-451, fda-esg.ts:376-390 (typed internal patch), AnaToolExecutor override_import_mapping 14987-15006. changeControl.service.ts:200-216/258-275 uses literal column names in add() calls.
(3) Booleans that select a fixed fragment: projects.ts:1532 (lock ? ' FOR UPDATE'), authoring-file-to-vault.ts:139 (hasProvenance ? ', provenance'), mdx-udi.ts:162 scoped(col) with a literal col and $2 (program_id is UUID-regex validated at :141), regulatory-correspondence.ts:1130 projectClause, which binds the value as $2.
(4) Constant SQL fragments and helpers called with literal aliases. completeStatusSqlList() re-checks each status against an identifier regex. WS_CASE / workstreamSqlCase builds from WORKSTREAM_FILING_TYPES constants. Also supersededSql('d'), uploadedBinaryAvailableSql('f'), capturedDataEligibleSql('src'), artifact*Sql('a'), IMPLEMENTATION_OVERDUE_SQL, ACTIVE_TRANSMITTAL_STATUSES, CITATION_IMAGE_COLUMNS, visibleOrgClause() (returns a fixed SQL string plus a bound org param). In recorded-lineage.ts, every alias goes through lineageAlias(), which applies the identifier regex at :9-11; kind is a 'captured'|'upload' union; MAX_RECORDED_DEPTH is a constant.
(5) Identifiers from code or the database catalog. signed-record.ts:135/145 takes table and statusColumn from the SIGNED_REGISTERS union-typed constants (caller api/cmc/routes.ts:838 passes a register object, never request text). tenant-storage.ts:144-145 takes table and column names from information_schema with a fixed key list, and table/sizeColumn are regex-checked. tenantColumn is limited to the TENANT_KEY_COLUMNS constants.
(6) projects.ts:2125 opts.set holds only literal strings (projects.ts:2155/2170/2182).
(7) AnaToolExecutor.ts:17186-17188 (CMC register lookup). searchCols are code constants; the search text is bound as an ILIKE parameter; LIMIT ${limit} is Number(), required finite and > 0, then Math.floor and capped at 100 (:17032-17033). A prototype key such as "constructor" passed as register would only cause an SQL error, not injection.
(8) knowledgeGraphService.ts:293-299 sends user-derived text to to_tsquery as a bound parameter. Bad input there can raise a syntax error but cannot inject.

verdicts.path: Sink at server/services/cognitive-ecosystem/checkpoint-manager.service.ts:537 splices checkpointId into a quoted jsonb literal with no escaping, so the code is injectable. Nothing calls forkFromCheckpoint: the only references to CheckpointManager outside its own file are langgraph-orchestrator.service.ts:32/122/354/751 (constructor, getTuple, put) and the barrel re-export in index.ts:12. LangGraphOrchestrator is imported only by the cognitive-ecosystem index barrel. server/routes/cognitive-ecosystem.ts:27-28 imports an empty list from that barrel and is not mounted (retired at server/bootstrap/register-document-routes.ts:253, #844). There is also a precondition: the bound SELECT at :515 has to find a stored row whose id contains the payload. The target table agent_runtime.checkpoints is created only by db/migrations/_legacy/063_gcc_cognitive_agent_runtime.sql:174, which is a legacy file, so in production that SELECT probably fails before the sink is reached. No HTTP request, tool call or job reaches this code.
verdicts.fix: Bind the value, e.g. context_data || jsonb_build_object('forked_from', $4::text), and pass checkpointId as $4. Better still, delete the unused cognitive-ecosystem service tree together with the retired router.

verdicts.path: Sink at checkpoint-manager.service.ts:197-199 interpolates each key of options.filter into c.metadata->>'${key}' unescaped (values are bound), so the code is injectable. In-repo callers use only getTuple (langgraph-orchestrator.service.ts:354) and put (:751). Nothing calls list(), and nothing calls it with a filter. The orchestrator itself is reachable only through the unmounted, retired /api/cognitive-ecosystem router (register-document-routes.ts:253), which imports nothing from the service. The schema it queries (agent_runtime) exists only in a _legacy migration. No production request can supply a filter key.
verdicts.fix: Bind the key, e.g. AND c.metadata->>$n = $m, or check it against /^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/ before building the string. Better still, delete the dead CheckpointManager and orchestrator.

verdicts.path: Sinks are server/services/cortexComplianceService.ts:369 and :447 (both `SELECT * FROM ${this.escapeTableName(...)} WHERE id = $1`), plus :677 and :830. escapeTableName (:937) applies only the regex /^[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+$/. That blocks syntax injection such as quotes, spaces, semicolons or comments, but it lets through any schema-qualified identifier (for example pg_catalog.pg_authid, or another tenant table), so if any caller passed it untrusted input it would be identifier injection. No production caller exists. A grep of server, shared and scripts finds CortexComplianceService and getCortexComplianceService referenced only by: the re-export barrel server/services/cortex/index.ts:22,28; server/services/index.ts:17 (`export * as cortex`), which nothing imports (the only `services` index import is ../../startup/services, a different module); a JSDoc comment in server/routes/cognitive-ecosystem.ts:18, which never imports the service; and server/__tests__/routes/smoke.test.ts:129, which only checks that the class can be exported. No router, tool or job constructs the service or calls createElectronicSignature, verifySignature, verifyRecordIntegrity or auditedDelete, so no HTTP request, tool call or job input reaches these sinks.
verdicts.fix: Delete the dead CortexComplianceService together with its barrel re-exports. If it is kept, replace escapeTableName's regex with a fixed allowlist map from record type to a code-constant table name, reject schema-qualified names, and add an organization_id predicate to the SELECT and UPDATE statements.

classify:11.safeSummary:
No suspects in shard 11. None of the 19 files uses drizzle sql.raw, sql.identifier, or sql`` templates; all SQL goes through pg pool/client .query(text, params). I classified 87 SQL-text interpolation sites. That is 79 template-literal sites found by a scanner and checked by hand, plus about 8 cases where the query is built in a variable and then passed to query(). All are safe, falling into these patterns:

(1) Placeholder indexes such as $${idx++}, $${paramIdx}, $${args.length}, $${params.length}, $${i + 3} and categories.length + 3. This covers manufacturing-routes, mdx-risk-management, command-executor list/search/history, context-enrichment, precedent-engine, rtf-trigger-service, adaptive-reviewer-workspace and evidence-objects, where q is bound as a %q% parameter.

(2) SET/column lists taken from hardcoded allowlists:
- mdx-risk-management.ts:226/364: COL map over zod-parsed keys (unknown keys are stripped).
- command-executor.ts:421/1216/2960: snakeKey must pass allowedFields.includes(...) exactly, so model-supplied update keys cannot inject.
- adaptive-reviewer-workspace and manufacturing: fixed column names per branch.

(3) Constant ternaries:
- ectd-compile.ts:227 and precedent-engine.ts:1204: byUuid/isUuid choose 'id = $1' or 'code = $1'.
- lumen-context-builder.ts:320: org clause.
- document-chunking-backfill.ts:102 and 159: retryFailed/embed choose between fixed fragments.
- authoring-permissions.ts:220: sectionPredicate with a bound $n.

(4) Code constants:
- ectd-compile loadAnchorSections columns/orderBy: only literal callers at :568/:1237/:1440, orderBy 'section_code'.
- precedent-engine loadPatternRows table/columns: only literal callers at :299/:315.
- document-data-disposition IMPACT_TABLES: const array.
- interview-sessions RETURNING: const.
- mdx-proactive-signals day constants (14/60/14) and deep-investigation PROGRESS_EVENT_CAP=60.
- vault SQL helpers (vaultDispositionChoiceSql/BinaryAvailable/DataEligible/supersededSql): called only with the literal alias 'd'.
- buildPrecedentOrgIsolation: emits only $n placeholders, and the org id is bound.

(5) Numeric LIMIT interpolation:
- study-design-evidence.service.ts:67 LIMIT ${limit}: limit = Math.min(Math.max(opts.limit ?? 50, 1), 200), which coerces to a number, and every caller passes a literal 50/100/200. The worst case is NaN, which is a syntax error, not an injection. Hardening note only: Number.isInteger would be cleaner.
- Keyword ILIKE terms in that file are bound as parameters.

Side observation, not SQL injection and out of scope: adaptive-reviewer-workspace-service.ts:~530 runs session-level SET app.bypass_rls='true' on a pooled client.
